title: spec(object-extension `fieldPatches`): the record key is a bare `z.string()`, so `fieldPatches: { Industry: {…} }` parses and is refused only downstream by the target judge
body:
domain:spec#1 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmPi25XXKx92Xmg4viS

Filing gate: ② should-fix 1 of the spec seat's contract review on PR #29331 (#28655), at head `5f8d7494`. ⛔ Not a claim. No grade: triage sets it.
Reader: `domain:spec`, `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts` (`ObjectExtensionSchema.fieldPatches`).

## What happens

PR #29331 keys a field patch's `options` map by `SelectOptionSchema.shape.value`, so an option key that can never be an option value is refused at the schema. `fieldPatches`' own record key is still `z.string()`, while a field name has a grammar (`FieldSchema.name` and the `ObjectSchema.fields` keys are snake_case). So `fieldPatches: { Industry: { label: 'Sector' } }` parses at the schema and is refused only later, by the target judge, as an unknown target. It is the same class as #28655's item B, and the same derivation is available: key the record by the schema that keys `ObjectSchema.fields`.

## Done when

`fieldPatches` is keyed by the field-name key schema `ObjectSchema.fields` uses, with an `invalid_key` issue and a prescription for a key outside the grammar. Measure first whether any authored form in examples, skills, docs or templates would newly refuse (if any: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` / `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, BREAKING; if the target judge already refuses every such key at every door, say so — the change may then be a location-only `semantic`).

Dedupe: #28655 / PR #29331 (items A–D, landing). **New.**
